objective.statement: Learn six more words of speed and character: allargando, grave, larghetto, giocoso, simile and vivo.
successCriteria: I can put grave, largo and larghetto in order from slowest to fastest.
I know allargando means broadening, and vivo means lively and quick.
I know giocoso means playful and simile means carry on in the same way.

explanation.text: Here are six more words. Grave, larghetto and allargando are about slow, broad music. Vivo is quick, like vivace. Giocoso describes a playful mood, and simile tells the player to carry on in the same way.

“allargando” means broadening: getting a little slower, and usually a little louder. “grave” means very slow and solemn. “larghetto” means rather slow, but not as slow as largo. “giocoso” means playful and merry.
“simile” means in the same way: carry on as before. “vivo” means lively and quick.
From slowest to fastest the slow words go grave, largo, larghetto. Allargando is different: it is a change, getting a little slower and broader, usually with a little more sound.

explanation.text: Slow: grave (very slow, solemn), largo (slow, stately), larghetto (rather slow). Changing: allargando (broadening). Quick: vivo. Mood: giocoso (playful). Carry on: simile.

steps: Look at the word above the first bar: larghetto.
It ends in -etto, which means a little: a little largo, so rather slow, but not as slow as largo.
Play it gently and broadly, but keep it moving.
